questions.stem: Find the mean of $4, 6, 8, 10, 12$.
questions.explanation: The mean of raw data is $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x}{n} = \frac{4 + 6 + 8 + 10 + 12}{5} = \frac{40}{5} = 8$. The five numbers are equally spaced, so the mean sits at the middle value.

distractorRationale.a: This is the second value, or the result of dividing the sum by $n + 1$
distractorRationale.c: This is the fourth value, not the mean
distractorRationale.d: This is $\sum x$, with the division by $n$ forgotten

questions.stem: Find the median of $4, 7, 9, 11, 14, 18$.
questions.explanation: There are $n = 6$ values, an even count, so the median is the average of the $\frac{n}{2}$th and $\left(\frac{n}{2} + 1\right)$th values — the 3rd and 4th. Those are $9$ and $11$, and $\frac{9 + 11}{2} = 10$.

distractorRationale.a: Took only the 3rd value, as if $n$ were odd
distractorRationale.c: Took only the 4th value
distractorRationale.d: Averaged $9$ with $10$, or used a half-position incorrectly

questions.stem: The marks of ten students are $4, 6, 6, 7, 8, 8, 8, 9, 9, 10$. Find the mean mark. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Sum the marks: $4 + 6 + 6 + 7 + 8 + 8 + 8 + 9 + 9 + 10 = 75$. Then $\bar{x} = \frac{75}{10} = 7.5$. The same result comes from the frequency form $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$ if the repeated scores are grouped first.

questions.stem:
The table shows the distribution of weekly savings (₦) of traders. Which is the modal class?

| Class (₦) | $1$–$10$ | $11$–$20$ | $21$–$30$ | $31$–$40$ |
| Frequency | $4$ | $9$ | $7$ | $5$ |
questions.explanation: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency. Here that frequency is $9$, so the modal class is $11$–$20$. Do not confuse the modal class with the class that contains the mean or the median.

distractorRationale.a: This is the first class, not the most frequent
distractorRationale.c: This class has the second-highest frequency
distractorRationale.d: This is the last class, not the modal class

questions.stem: Estimate the mean of the grouped data: class $0$–$10$ has frequency $3$, class $10$–$20$ has frequency $5$, and class $20$–$30$ has frequency $2$. Use class midpoints. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: The midpoints are $5$, $15$ and $25$. Then $\sum f x_m = 3(5) + 5(15) + 2(25) = 15 + 75 + 50 = 140$ and $\sum f = 10$, so $\bar{x} = \frac{140}{10} = 14$. This is an estimate because every value in a class is represented by the midpoint.

questions.stem:
The table shows the scores of $25$ students.

| Score ($x$) | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ |
| Frequency ($f$) | $3$ | $5$ | $8$ | $6$ | $3$ |

The median score is
questions.explanation: For ungrouped frequency data with $n = 25$ (odd), the median is the $\frac{n + 1}{2} = 13$th value. The cumulative frequencies are $3$, $8$, $16$, $22$ and $25$, so the 13th value lies in the score $4$. The mode is also $4$, but that is a coincidence — the median is located by position, not by the tallest frequency.

distractorRationale.a: Stopped in the class whose cumulative frequency is $8$, before reaching the 13th value
distractorRationale.c: Took the next class after the median position
distractorRationale.d: Gave the highest frequency rather than the median score
